newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine 1997 barley crop seen up on 1996.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine 1997 barley crop seen up on 1996.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE: BARLEY CROP IN 1997 SEEN RECOVERING TO 7.5-8.0 MLN T
MOSCOW, May 14 - Total Ukrainian barley output in 1997 is forecast to rise to 7.5 to 8.0 million tonnes from 5.7 million tonnes in 1996's drought-hit harvest.
Around 45 percent of barley and oats have been sown with a one-month delay, possibly resulting in a 15-percent decline in yields.

The recovery in barley production will lead to an increase in Ukraine's barley exports. SovEcon and Ukragroconsult tentatively peg Ukraine's barley exports in 1997/98 in a range of 0.6-1.0 million tonnes against 0.4 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Ukrainian farmers had planted 4.3 million hectares to spring grains and pulses by May 5, ahead of last year's delayed sowing campaign but still well behind normal levels.
The total area sown to spring grains and pulses is expected to increase by 15 percent to about 5 million hectares, roughly at last year's levels.
